analysis:
All three changed files are test-only, under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests. They add CoordinatorReconnectPolicyTests.swift, NetworkFrameworkCloseCodeTests.swift, and a parameterized MockCoordinator.dropActiveWebSocket(closeCode:reason:) at MockCoordinator.swift lines 445-456 on the head side. The production types they exercise (CoordinatorReconnectPolicy, CoordinatorSessionEnd, sentCloseCode, CoordinatorClient runLoop) are not in the supplied diff. Their implementation is therefore unreviewed and is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.

The tests assert the reconnect policy: backoff resets after a session open 60 s or longer, close code 1012 gives a 0-1 s wait without growing the backoff, and every other end keeps the existing exponential backoff. This touches TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket) availability. A hostile or compromised coordinator or edge could send 1012 close codes to force fast reconnect loops, since 1012 waits 0-1 s with no growth. The impact is limited to reconnect rate against the coordinator the provider already trusts. Provider-side load or abuse of the coordinator is a denial-of-service consideration for the next pass. The production policy should be checked to confirm that repeated 1012 closes stay bounded, for example that the registration and attestation path is not hammered. No mitigation is visible in the supplied files.

The mock helper only runs on loopback 127.0.0.1 with port 0 and handles no secrets. The network tests use a plain ws:// NWConnection against the local mock, with no TLS or credential handling. The default reason string and the default close code 1001 preserve the previous behaviour. No change touches attestation, encryption, A-003, A-008 or prefix-cache storage, so T-041 and the App Attest threat entries (TB-011) are unaffected.

No findings. The production reconnect policy code is not in this batch, so a deeper review of it is requested.
